title: The End of Time Management: Illusions and Italians
coreMove: Stop managing every hour; use 80/20 to choose the few actions that matter, then use Parkinson's Law to keep those actions from swelling.

exampleSpecs.audience: Gerald, an operations lead sorting product lines
exampleSpecs.stakes: Slow movers crowd out the products that drive shipment value.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Pareto's uneven distribution to cut low-return inventory work.

exampleSpecs.audience: Pierre, a sales director trimming a bloated proposal process
exampleSpecs.stakes: A buyer needs a clear offer while the team wants another week of polish.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply Parkinson's Law only after the valuable sales task has been selected.

exampleSpecs.audience: Everly, a customer success manager ranking accounts by burden
exampleSpecs.stakes: High-noise accounts consume the week while better accounts wait.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rank customers by return and stress, then decide which customers should change or leave.

exampleSpecs.audience: Bryan, a program director choosing a grant draft scope
exampleSpecs.stakes: A small grant needs a usable draft, not a week of internal theater.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Recover from a bloated deadline by compressing a selected priority.

exampleSpecs.audience: Delaney, a product lead cutting a crowded roadmap
exampleSpecs.stakes: Low-use features drain engineers from the fixes customers actually value.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use uneven feature return to remove roadmap items rather than optimize all of them.

exampleSpecs.audience: Laurence, an attorney narrowing a status brief
exampleSpecs.stakes: A judge needs the issue and next action, while the team keeps adding background.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show useful compression without confusing it with reckless haste.
